**⚠⚠ THE PAIR-WALK COUNT IS THE PROOF THAT IS NOT A RATIO.** `browser/a11y.spec.ts` walks the kit fixture and counts DISTINCT RENDERED COLOUR PAIRS, deduping by colour rather than by role. Dark went **11 → 12**, and the entry that appeared is `#FCFCFA on #191C22` — `ink` on the product's own ground. Until this ticket that pair and the ready screen's `#FCFCFA on #0A1F17` **were the same two colours**, so the walk counted them once. They are two entries now. That is `R-249`'s mechanism expressed as an integer, and it was named by re-running the walk with the assertion widened to print both lists rather than by reasoning about it.

**⚠⚠ AND `R-249`'s CLOSURE NAMES ITS OWN LIMIT.** The two grounds are **1.00:1** — `ink` and `ready-field` differ in HUE and are identical in VALUE — and a dichromat simulation (Viénot 1999 on linear RGB) moves that only to **1.18** for deuteranopia and protanopia. So the ready screen is no longer the same field as everything else, and it is still announced by `signal` and the button rather than by its field. That residual is **`R-257`**, raised in the same change rather than folded into the closure.

**THE DEFAULT WAS NOT A DEFAULT, AND NO TEST COULD HAVE SEEN IT.** `ThemeProvider` already defaulted to `theme='light'` and rendered `data-theme="light"` — on a **div**, because a React provider cannot own the document element — while the generated stylesheet guarded its dark media query on `:root:not([data-theme='light'])`, which reads `<html>`. The guard never matched. **Measured with Playwright at `prefers-color-scheme: dark`: `/staff` rendered `--color-paper: #191C22` and a card at `rgb(43, 46, 51)` while the element carried `data-theme="light"`.** The suite asserts the ATTRIBUTE, and the attribute was correct the whole time; it took rendering the page in a browser with a dark preference and reading the resolved custom property. The generator now emits a `[data-theme='light']` block, and the same probe after the fix reads light under both schemes.

**⚠⚠⚠ THE E2E ROUND TOOK FIVE RUNS AND THE MIDDLE TWO ARE THE ONES WORTH READING, BECAUSE THEY ARE A FIX THAT WAS TRIED AND REVERTED.** Runs 1 and 2 were `R-256` — a staff screen's marker never appearing inside 60 s, on two different cases in two different browsers. ⚠ **The mechanism was then MEASURED rather than suspected**, from Playwright's own page snapshot: the view had mounted and was stuck on `status: جارٍ التحميل`, so the nav click worked and the data request did not answer. That is a queue, and `tools/browsers/bin/e2e` serves the API from a **single-process** `php artisan serve` against five parallel browser projects. So the harness was given **eight workers and `--no-reload`** (which `ServeCommand` requires, or it warns and makes one server anyway). **It worked on its own terms — neither run under it reproduced a marker timeout — and it broke something worse:** `staff.spec.ts:672` *locks the shell after idle, and the session is dead on the server afterwards* went red on `staff-chromium-ltr` in **both** runs (15.3s, then 14.3s, *"the server session survived the lock"*, 200 where 401 was required), a case that had passed in the two runs before it. **Reverted, and run 5 is green at 531 / 16 / 0** — which also confirms the attribution in both directions. Sessions are in Redis, so a per-process store is not the explanation; the investigation stops there because this is not `QRPAGER-39`'s ticket. **What `R-256` now carries is a measured cause and a ruled-out remedy**, which is worth more than another re-run.

⚠ **`R-250` OCCURRED A SECOND TIME IN TWO DAYS AND IS STILL NOT FIXED.** `ticket-tables.test.mjs` forced five cells of **Task 8a's delivered ticket** to be rewritten because the live palette moved; the edit is kept with a dated note, under Muhammad's ruling of 2026-11-08. **ONLY THE FRAMING CLAUSE MOVED, AND THAT IS A CONTROL RATHER THAN A CLAIM.**

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `X-Frame-Options` | `DENY` | **`SAMEORIGIN`** |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | `default-src 'none'; img-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; `**`frame-ancestors 'none'`**`; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'` | `default-src 'none'; img-src 'self'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; `**`frame-ancestors 'self'`**`; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'none'` |

`PreviewFramingTest` parses both policies into directive sets and requires the difference to be **exactly one entry** — `['frame-ancestors' => "'none' -> 'self'"]`. A future change that relaxes `default-src` or `form-action` while editing the framing names the directive that moved, instead of passing because the framing assertion still matches.

**THE FOURTH CASE REFUSES WHAT THE DIRECTIVE MAY *BECOME*, WHICH THE OTHER THREE CANNOT.** `ReviewFixesTest` and `ResponseHeaderTest` assert the value IS `'self'` — and `toContain("frame-ancestors 'self'")` would pass a widening to `'self' https://evil.test`. The new case asserts the whole value is `'self'` and nothing else: no wildcard, no second source, no scheme, not absent, and not back to `'none'`. Four separate assertions, so a failure names which widening happened.

**⚠⚠ AND `HardenResponse` WAS OVERWRITING THE HEADER THREE LINES LATER — FOUND BY THE NEW TEST, NOT BY READING THE FILE.** It set `X-Frame-Options: DENY` unconditionally, deliberately, *"so a controller cannot weaken one of these by accident"*. Left alone, the two headers would have DISAGREED about who may frame a tenant's draft — CSP permitting the panel, the legacy header refusing it — and the pane would have been blank in every engine that reads the older one. The header is now **derived from the response's own `frame-ancestors`**: `'self'` exactly, as the whole value, or `DENY`. ⚠ **Not a path allowlist**, which would have been a second place to keep in step with `PreviewController` and which `R-242`'s ruling makes expensive on purpose: the two headers answer the same question, so the modern one decides and the legacy one follows. A controller gets `SAMEORIGIN` only by having set a same-origin policy itself, so the property the original comment claims is intact.

**WHAT IS STILL REFUSED, stated because a reader of the diff will ask:** every cross-origin framer (clickjacking needs one); script of any origin, framed or not, since `default-src 'none'` did not move; and the `§11` finding itself, whose subject was draft bytes on the session-bearing origin under a weaker policy than the image inside them — `default-src`, `img-src`, `style-src`, `base-uri` and `form-action` are byte-identical to what that review left.

**⚠ CONDITION 3 OF THE RULING IS UNMEASURED AND SAYS SO.** It asks for the minimum `sandbox` token set that still renders the draft's images and inline styles, **measured in the booted panel**. The pane does not exist yet, so there is nothing to measure; guessing a token set is the one thing that condition forbids. It is sequencing rather than a gap — Muhammad's own words — and it is the first thing the rebuild owes.

**WHAT THIS PR DOES NOT CONTAIN, so nobody reads the branch name and expects it:** the four tabs, the Theme and Search-and-sharing move, the preview pane, the numbered running order, the status plate, the footer bar, the before/after capability list and the per-tab save test. ⚠ **AND ONE DEFECT FOUND BY READING BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN:** `LandingBuilderPage::save()` builds the whole document from its own form state, and `StudioForm::toDocument()` reads the theme values out of that same flat state — so moving Theme out of that form would make **every save from the page tab write a document with `theme` empty**, deleting a tenant's theme by saving a block. The fix is for each page to merge its own form state over the stored draft before building the document, and Muhammad's ruling is that it **does not land without its test in the same commit**, both directions, per tab.

⚠ **`gate:e2e` IS NOT ONE OF THE THREE GATE FIGURES AND ITS STATE IS REPORTED ANYWAY.** Two full journey runs on this tree: **533 passed / 16 skipped / 1 failed**, both times, and a DIFFERENT staff case each time (`staff.spec.ts:1071` `staff-firefox-ltr`, then `:798` `staff-chromium-rtl`). Both are `R-256`'s family — a staff screen's marker failing to appear inside 60 s under the run's own load — and that row now carries four occurrences across runs that bracket this ticket's harness change on both sides, which is what shows the change is not their cause. **Part B's own three cases passed in every run**, including a dedicated `--project=studio-chromium` run of 3/3.

⚠⚠ **EVERY ITEM WAS MEASURED IN THE BOOTED PANEL BEFORE IT WAS CHANGED, AND THREE OF THE MEASUREMENTS CHANGED THE FIX.**

**Item 3 — the sizes were already on the scale; the HIERARCHY was not.** Measured at 1280px: page heading 44px, tab label 16, section heading 16, legend 16, radio option 13, button 13. Three different roles all landed on 16, the title jumped straight to the 44 DISPLAY step, and the two middle steps the scale exists to provide — 20 and 28 — were rendered by nothing. So "unrelated sizes" was not off-scale values; it was a missing middle. ⚠ **And the first version of that block named three classes Filament does not render** (`fi-fo-radio-option-label`, `fi-fo-field-wrp-label`, `fi-fo-field-wrp-hint`), so it changed nothing — the screenshot said so, and the real names were read off the DOM: `.fi-fo-field-label` was **13px**, a field's own name at the helper step.

**Item 3 again — "the radio labels crowd their controls" is not a gap problem.** Measured: the input sits at x=1228 w=44 and the option text ends at x=1216, a gap of exactly **12px**, which is a step of the ladder and correct. The fault was the CROSS axis — `align-items: normal` stretched the text beside a 44px control so its first line sat at the top of the box. Centring was the whole fix, and the gap a reading would have changed was left alone.

**Item 6 — the first probe said the panel was painted in Filament's greys, and it was wrong.** `--color-surface` resolves to the SHORTHAND `#fff`, and a string compare against `#ffffff` reported every white surface in the panel as off-palette. Normalising three-digit hex first took the finding from "the panel is painted in Filament's greys" to **1 off-token colour in light and 4 in dark** — and the real defect is narrower and worse than greys: the INHERITED text colour was a browser default in both modes (`#000000` / `#ffffff`) while `ink` is `#191c22` / `#fcfcfa`.

⚠ **AND THE DARK FIX IS ONE VARIABLE, READ OUT OF THE COMPILED THEME.** Twelve elements painted `#ffffff` in dark. Chasing them class by class would be twelve rules that go stale the moment Filament renames one; the compiled stylesheet says `.dark,.dark *){color:var(--color-white)`, so the panel redefines `--color-white` for itself and every rule referencing it resolves to the token — including rules this stylesheet has never heard of. Scoped to `.dark`, because that variable is also what `bg-white` resolves to.

⚠ **`html` WAS THE LAST ONE, AND ONLY A WALK COULD FIND IT.** `fi-panel-studio` is on `body`, so a rule scoped to it leaves the ROOT element on the UA default. Nothing visible inherits from `html` once `body` sets a colour — which is exactly why reading the file would not find it, and why walking every element reported `color #000000 on html.fi` as the one value left.

⚠⚠ **FOUR GUARDS REFUSED THIS WORK AND ALL FOUR WERE RIGHT.** `scan-panel` refused five hexes in `ColourField`'s PROSE — `R-260` happening to the same author in the same week — and refused a mid-grey default written into panel PHP, which is a design decision made outside the token layer. `PanelTargetTest` refused `fi-valid` on the new swatch: a validity state is not a control and covering it would floor everything that carries one — and the swatch was **48x32**, under the bar, in a brand-new control on the tab that exists for it. `lint-scope` refused a 23rd Playwright project until a human looked at it. And `RepoGuardTest` had already refused a raw Blade echo in part A.

⚠⚠⚠ **`R-264`: NO BROWSER TEST COULD EXERCISE A FILAMENT PANEL AT ALL, AND TWO OF PART B'S OWN CASES WERE LYING BECAUSE OF IT.** The e2e TLS front forwards over plain http and stated adding no header as a virtue, so the API generated `http://` asset URLs for an `https://` page and the panel's own CSP blocked its theme, all seven Filament bundles and Livewire. The colour case reported **131 off-token colours**, every one a browser default, pointing squarely at the token layer and about nothing of the sort; the sticky case **PASSED**, because with no CSS `position` resolved to `static` and the pane merely happened to sit in the viewport. Both now assert their own premise first — that the theme loaded, and that `position` is `sticky` — and the harness says it terminated TLS. Nothing was wrong with the application: `TrustProxies` is on its global stack and `BootChecks` refuses a catch-all trust list.

**+8 cases and +30 assertions over `main`'s 1439 / 13,801**, which is this part's test file exactly and nothing else — the conversion itself moved no count, because `en` carries the strings character for character and every service-level test still reads the sentence it always read.

⚠⚠ **THE MEASUREMENT THAT SET THE SCOPE, TAKEN BEFORE ANY CODE WAS WRITTEN.** There was no localization layer at all: **no `lang/` directory, exactly ONE `__()` call in the entire application** (`resources/views/errors/panel-problem.blade.php`), `'locale' => env('APP_LOCALE', 'en')`, and **`setLocale` called nowhere**. So item 1 was build-the-mechanism plus ~90 strings. Reported to Muhammad, who re-scoped the ticket on it.

**AND THE OTHER HALF OF THAT MEASUREMENT PAID FOR ITSELF:** all ten Filament packages ship `resources/lang/ar`, so `Collapse all`, `Expand all`, the block picker, clone, delete, edit, reorder and move up/down translate from the locale alone. They are **not** in `lang/{ar,en}/studio.php`, and re-stating one there would create a second source for a string the framework already owns.

**ONE CALL TURNS ON THREE THINGS.** `StudioLocale` sets the application locale from `tenants.language`, and that alone gives: (1) Filament's chrome in Arabic, above; (2) `<html dir="rtl">`, because `filament-panels::layout.direction` is `rtl` in that package's `ar` file and `base.blade.php` reads it — the property `PlatformPanelAccessibilityTest` already proved on the other panel; (3) `StudioForm`'s `$t->label(app()->getLocale())`, **a call site that has been correct since `QRPAGER-33` and had never once reached its Arabic branch**, because the locale was never anything but `en`.

⚠⚠ **A MIDDLEWARE IS NOT ENOUGH, AND THIS CODEBASE ALREADY KNEW WHY.** `TenantPanelAccess`'s docblock records Task 6's security M-1: *"`POST /livewire-<hash>/update` runs neither `SetUpPanel` nor Filament's `Authenticate`"*. Confirmed again with `route:list` — that route carries `['web', RequireLivewireHeaders]` and not the panel's stack. So the middleware covers the full-page GET and **nothing else**: every notification raised by `save`, `publish`, `unpublish`, `store`, `delete`, `add` and `advance` would have rendered in English inside an Arabic panel, **invisible in any screenshot of a resting page**, appearing the first time the owner pressed a button. `HasStudioLocale` closes it with Livewire's own `boot{TraitName}` hook, which runs on every request a component serves. **A TEST SAID SO, NOT A READING:** `StudioActionsTest`'s publish-failure case drives the page through `Livewire::test()`, asserted the Arabic headline and got the English one.

⚠⚠ **TWO DEFECTS THE ENUMERATION FOUND THAT NO REVIEW WOULD HAVE.**

**(1) ALL TWELVE THEME LABELS RENDERED AS THEIR OWN KEYS.** `ThemeTokens::NAMES` is keyed `color.background`, Laravel reads a dot as a path, and a flat `'color.background'` inside `tokens` is never reached by that descent. **The miss is silent — Laravel returns the key** — so the theme tab displayed the literal text `studio.tokens.color.background` as a field label. The keys are nested now.

**(2) FILAMENT'S ARABIC IS INCOMPLETE — `R-263`.** Measured by diffing the `en` and `ar` key sets of every package used here: **41 keys missing**, plus one file that does not exist. Four are rendered by the studio, and **three of them are the block list's screen-reader announcements** — an Arabic owner reordering his page heard *"Block, position 2 of 7"* in English, on the running order `QRPAGER-40` built, in a panel `§12` exempts from the visual bar and never from the accessibility bar. Overridden in `lang/vendor/filament-forms/ar/components.php`; the other 37 belong to components this panel does not use and are deliberately left.

**THE GATE IS FALSIFIABLE AND WAS FALSIFIED.** Muhammad asked for *"a test that fails on an unlocalized string, not a translation pass somebody has to re-audit by eye"*, and to prove it reddens by removing one key. Measured with `studio.page.status_heading` deleted from `ar/studio.php`: **two independent cases caught it** — the enumeration reported `/studio: Status`, and the parity check named `page.status_heading`. Restored, 8 passed.

**THE FIXTURE IS ARABIC, AND THAT IS WHAT MAKES THE ALLOW-LIST SHORT.** `LandingFixtures::fullPage()` is authored in English — *"Welcome to Olive"*, *"Find us"* — and those words render as each block row's summary; `TestCase::actingForTenant` names every user `Acting Staff`, which the panel prints in its user menu on all four tabs. Enumerating against either reports **the restaurant's own words as untranslated panel copy**. So the test authors its page in Arabic (over `authoredTextPaths()`, so a field added later is covered without an edit) and renames the acting account. The alternative was allow-listing `/^(Acting|Staff)$/` and `Welcome`, which is a hole through the middle of the one test that measures this.

⚠ **`StudioForm::label()` IS DELETED RATHER THAN KEPT AS A FALLBACK.** It was `ucfirst(str_replace(['_', '.'], ' ', $name))` — every field label DERIVED from the contract's field name, which is why the theme tab said *"Color background"*: nobody wrote those words. **A derived label cannot be translated**, so the names became keys. The derivation gave totality for free and a lookup does not, so `StudioLocalizationTest` requires a key per field in `BlockSchema` and per token in `ThemeTokens::NAMES`, in both languages. A fallback would have turned a missing key back into an English label appearing silently — the defect this ticket exists to remove.

⚠ **THE REFUSALS MOVED TOO, AND THE LINE IS AT THE LAYER BOUNDARY.** `MediaRejected`, `DomainRefused` and `PublishFailed` carry sentences whose own docblocks say they exist to be shown; they are in `lang/{ar,en}/landing.php` now, because `App\Features` may call `__()`. **`LandingDocumentInvalid` is not** — it is in `app/Domain`, which imports nothing but PHP built-ins, and `deptrac` rule 1 is *"domain logic imports no framework"*. Its notification also reads *"`blocks.0.fields.heading` can't be published: is required"*, so translating *"is required"* fixes the smaller half. **`R-262`** carries the design: a machine-readable `code` on the exception, resolved in the panel, with the field path turned into the block's name and the field's label.

⚠ **`PublishFailed`'s TWO HEADLINES ARE TRANSLATION KEYS NOW, NOT SENTENCES.** A class constant is evaluated at class load and can hold no `__()` call, so a sentence there could never follow a per-request locale. The two call sites that compare a headline compare against the constant and are unaffected by what it holds, so the distinction the class exists to make is untouched.

⚠⚠ **TWO REAL REDS OF THIS PART'S OWN MAKING, BOTH THE GATE WORKING.**

**`RepoGuardTest` refused a raw Blade echo.** The hostname is emphasised INSIDE a translated sentence, and I wrote it as `{!! __('…', ['hostname' => '<strong>'.e($h).'</strong>']) !!}` with a comment arguing the interpolation was pre-escaped. The guard's property is stronger and its own comment says why: *"No view in this application performs a raw echo. That is a stronger property than the one-exception version"* — and it is, because **the next person reaching for `{!! !!}` will also have a comment**. `studio/partials/emphasised.blade.php` splits the translated sentence on its own `:placeholder` and echoes every part with `{{ }}`: nothing is raw, and the emphasis lands where the TRANSLATOR put it rather than where English puts it, which three nodes in the view could not do.

**`PHPStan` refused `__()` into `helperText()`.** `__()` is typed `array|string|null` because a key may address a nested array — `studio.tokens` is exactly such a key — so the checker is right. `StudioForm::line()` resolves it with a real runtime check and a defined outcome (a non-string returns the key, which renders visibly), not a cast, an assert or a widened type.

**THE GATE'S INVARIANT IS A TEST AND THE LIST IS DERIVED, NEVER TYPED.** The ticket asks that every task the owner could do before, he can still do after — *"prove it with a list of them before and after, as a test"*. The AFTER side is read out of `BlockSchema`, `ThemeTokens` and the rendered pages at run time; only the BEFORE side is written down, as a frozen snapshot of what the single form offered, which is a historical fact and cannot drift. ⚠ **AND IT IS A FLOOR, NOT AN EQUALITY** — the claim is that nothing is LOST, so a later ticket adding a field must not fail it. An equality would turn this gate into an obstacle and get it deleted.

⚠⚠ **THREE THINGS THAT TEST GOT WRONG FIRST, EACH FIXED BY BEING RED, AND THEY ARE THE USEFUL PART.** (1) The BEFORE block list was written from MEMORY and named four types that do not exist — `about`, `menu`, `hours`, `map` — and is now read out of `git show 55a3a34:…/BlockType.php`. (2) `toContain` is **variadic** and read the failure message as another needle, which this repository has been bitten by before and which its own notes warn about. (3) Walking Filament's component tree does not work and cannot be made to — a `Section` outside a container throws from `BelongsToContainer`, and once bound, descending needs a Livewire component (*"getLivewire(): Return value must be of type Livewire\Component, null returned"*). So the cases **drive the pages over HTTP**, which is the better test anyway: the claim is about what the owner can see and type into, not about objects in a tree.

**THE DATA-LOSS DEFECT, FOUND BY READING BEFORE ANY OF IT WAS WRITTEN.** `StudioForm::toDocument()` builds the whole document — blocks, template, theme, seo — out of ONE flat state array, by key. Splitting the schema across two tabs without changing how they save means each tab deletes what the other owns: a save from `الصفحة` writes `theme` empty, a save from `الثيم` writes `blocks` empty. Silent both ways and **invisible in any screenshot**. `StudioForm::merged()` lays a page's state over the stored draft; `StudioDraftMergeTest` drives both directions per tab plus a third case that drives a real EDIT through each, because a `merged()` that ignored the incoming state would pass the first two perfectly by never changing anything. **Proven to redden: 3 failed (8 assertions) with the merge removed, 3 passed (11) with it restored.** `array_replace` and not `array_merge`, because `blocks` is keyed by order index and `array_merge` would silently reindex a tenant's page.

**CONDITION 3 OF THE FRAMING RULING, MEASURED IN THE BOOTED PANEL.**

| `sandbox` | frame reachable from the parent | renders |
| --- | --- | --- |
| absent | yes | title and inline styles present |
| `""` | **no — the frame has an OPAQUE ORIGIN** | — |
| `"allow-same-origin"` | yes | title and inline styles present |
| `"allow-same-origin allow-scripts"` | yes | title and inline styles present |

The bare attribute is the only one that protects anything, and it is the one that takes the frame's origin away — which matters because the preview's own policy is `img-src 'self'`, and against an opaque origin `'self'` matches nothing, so the tenant's images cannot load. Putting `allow-same-origin` back hands the origin over again and buys nothing `default-src 'none'` does not already give. **No token set both preserves the render and adds protection, so the attribute is omitted** — which is what the ruling said to do if that turned out to be the answer.

**⚠ `ember` AND `tile` ARE DEFERRED, NOT DROPPED.** `rail` ships as the only preset and is the default for a new restaurant. The reason is arithmetic rather than taste: the contract expresses **six** colours — `background`, `surface`, `text`, `muted`, `accent`, `accent_text` of `ThemeTokens::NAMES`'s twelve — and measured against the three reference files, **`ember` needs nine and `tile` ten** (14 and 13 distinct hexes, of which 0 and 2 map to the token layer, discounting four image slots each). `rail` translates **completely**, with no new colour token: 9 of its 15 map directly, four are image slots rather than colours, and its last two are a DARK FOOTER inside a light page — `#B5B8BF` and `#3A3D44` are hand-approximations of dark `ink-mid` and dark `hairline`, so the footer carries `data-theme="dark"` and uses the ordinary tokens. Light `ink-mid` on that ground measures ~2.8:1 and would fail AA, which is the proof the reference was right. The path forward is `§1`'s preset ruling: presets are tenant data, so `ThemeTokens::NAMES` widens at the preset ticket, never the token source.

**THE JUDGEMENT CALLS, EACH ACCEPTED ON ITS MERITS.** `aria-current="page"` over `role="tab"` — each tab is a separate page with its own URL and Livewire state, so they are NAVIGATION, and `role="tab"` would promise a screen-reader user that the panels are in this document and that arrow keys move between them. **`26rem` over the reference's `440px`** — the pane holds a 390px phone frame plus its hairline and padding without the form dropping under a comfortable measure at 1280px, which is the width the studio is used at; `--studio-frame-phone: 390px` is not a new number but the device width `browser/one-handed.spec.ts` already drives. Both live in **one layout-constants block at the top of the studio theme's layout rules**, per `§1`'s ruling that a one-off dimension is a layout constant rather than a token.

**THE NUMBER IN THE RUNNING ORDER IS A CSS COUNTER IN `arabic-indic`, AND THAT IS WHY IT IS CORRECT.** The ticket asks for the block's position ON THE PAGE; a number written into the markup is stale the moment a row is dragged and would need a round trip to fix. A counter is recomputed by the engine on every reflow. Filament's own block numbering is turned off, or each row carried two.

**⚠ SEVEN ENUMERATIONS WENT RED AND EVERY ONE WAS A CONTROL WORKING.** `StudioPanelInvariantTest`'s three route tables, `PanelThemeTest`'s chrome map, `PanelWalkTest`'s route list and title count, `PanelTargetTest`'s and `PanelAccessibilityFixtureTest`'s chrome floors, and `RouteSurfaceTest`'s public-surface allowlist — which caught `/studio/theme` as a **REAL red with 0 attributed**. An eighth panel route arriving silently is exactly what they exist to refuse.

**CARRIED, NOT FIXED — AND DELIBERATELY SO.** `LandingBuilderPage::mount()` fills its form from the whole document, so Livewire serialises theme values into the page tab's snapshot although no control renders them. Harmless to the tenant's data, because the save merges from the DATABASE and never from the snapshot; it means the page round-trips values it cannot edit. Muhammad's instruction was to leave it recorded where it is — in `StudioCapabilityTest`'s own docblock, beside the assertion that had to work around it — and not to fix it here.

⚠⚠ **QA 3 IS THE ONE WORTH READING, BECAUSE THE FIRST FIX FOR IT WAS ALSO DEAD.** The reviewer's own falsification was invalid — they renamed `fi-fo-field-label` in `field-wrapper.blade.php`, and Filament 5 renders this wrapper from a COMPILED copy in `vendor/filament/forms/src/Components/Field.php`, so the edit changed no output and could not have reddened anything. **The finding was right anyway.** Re-run against the compiled renderer, the strengthened assertion ALSO stayed green, because `\bfi-fo-field-label\b` matches inside `fi-fo-field-label-col`: `-` is a non-word character, so `\b` is satisfied by the wrapper's own column class sitting right beside the one the selector needs. The assertion written to close a dead control was a second dead control. It now uses `(?<![-\w])…(?![-\w])` and is proven in both directions against `Field.php:497`.

⚠ **QA 11, ANSWERED: THE CONTROL CLUSTER CANNOT SHRINK, AND ITS REASON IS NOT THE RADIO'S.** The ticket asks for *“the block row height and its control cluster”*. The cluster is five `.fi-icon-btn` at 44x44 from `targets.css`. Muhammad's ruling separated a 44px TARGET from a painted size **for a control Filament wraps in a `<label>`** — the row is the target, so the circle may be smaller. **An icon button has no such wrapper: its own box IS the pointer target**, so shrinking it shrinks the target, which is the waiver `§12` does not allow and the ruling explicitly was not. So the cluster stays at 44 and the row height is floored by it at 48. That is the ticket's *“STOP and report which”* for item A's third bullet, and it is now MEASURED rather than argued: the new block-row case asserts the row is 48 **and** that every button in it is still at least 44.

⚠ **TWO REDS ON THE WAY, NEITHER THIS DIFF'S AND NEITHER RE-RUN PAST.** `R-259` on `pnpm gate` attempts 1-2 — the first run in which both of its bounds failed together, `expected 91600 to be less than 15000` and `expected -71579 to be greater than or equal to 8500`, with the file passing 37/37 alone. `R-256` on `gate:e2e` run 1 — and the first occurrence that is NOT after a nav click: `[data-staff-shell="true"]` timed out inside `signInAsStaff()` itself, so `staff.spec.ts:128`'s own 44px assertion never ran. ### `QRPAGER-45` — **the preview follows the form, with no Save**, built 2026-11-11 on `qrpager-45/live-preview`, **REJECTED on delivery, fixed, merged as `114dbd0` (PR #18) — and its records repaired afterwards on `qrpager-45/record-repair`**

The ticket's stated invariant, in Muhammad's words: *"changing the arrangement, or editing a block field, is reflected in the preview with no Save click and no page refresh — proven by a browser test asserting the preview CONTENT changed, not that a reload was requested."*

⚠⚠ **THAT INVARIANT IS SUPERSEDED, AND IT IS SUPERSEDED BECAUSE IT IS WHAT LET THE DELIVERY SHIP BROKEN.** It names *builder-page* controls — an arrangement, a block field — and the studio has a SECOND page that writes the same document. `previewChanged()` and both `forget()` calls lived on `LandingBuilderPage` alone, so **a colour saved on `الثيم` never reached the preview**: the key written while the owner was on the builder tab kept winning over the draft they had just saved, and the only thing that cleared it was the arrangement control, whose write rebuilds the whole document from one flat state and carried the new theme in **by accident**. Muhammad rejected the delivery on 2026-11-11 and ruled the shape of the fix in the same message: *"fix at the SHARED level, not per page. Whatever the preview contract is — write on settled change, forget on save and publish — both studio pages implement it."* **A ticket's invariant can be satisfied and its subject still broken; this one was, and the test suite agreed with the invariant rather than with the product.**

**THE AMENDED INVARIANT, which REPLACES the one above wherever this ticket is cited:**

> On every studio page, a settled change is reflected in the preview with no Save click and no page refresh; and after a save on any studio page, the preview and the stored draft agree.

The second clause is the one that was violated and the one nothing tested. It lives in `app/Features/Landing/Panel/KeepsPreviewInStep.php` — one trait, both pages — with `resources/views/studio/partials/preview-sync.blade.php` carrying the debounce for every page that includes it, and `StudioPreviewContractTest` asserting that **every page the panel registers** which can write the draft implements it.

⚠ **FOURTEEN FALSIFICATIONS, EACH RUN AND EACH NAMED — six from the build, eight from the rejection and the rounds.** Every specification of this ticket has a case that reddens when it is undone, and *when* matters here: the first six were measured against a delivery that was then **rejected for a bug none of them could see**, which is what the other eight are for.

⚠⚠ **THREE DEFECTS IN THIS TICKET'S OWN CODE, ALL FOUND BY TESTS AND NONE BY READING.**

1. **`catch (Throwable)` MADE THE UUID GUARD UNREACHABLE.** `get()` built the key inside the try, so `InvalidArgumentException` was swallowed exactly like a dead socket and a malformed tenant id returned *"nothing to show"* instead of refusing. The control that exists to keep a key PATTERN out of Redis could not fire. Same shape as the broad catches the `§11` round of `QRPAGER-44` found a day earlier.
2. **`getState()` RUNS FILAMENT'S VALIDATION BEFORE THE DOCUMENT GATE.** A required field the owner has just emptied throws `ValidationException`, not `LandingDocumentInvalid` — and uncaught, on a method that fires behind every keystroke, that is a user-facing error bag. One of the two ways to be invalid was raising.
3. **`save()` AND `publish()` FORGOT THE KEY AND DISPATCHED NO RELOAD.** Removing the key means the NEXT render shows the stored draft, but nothing was asking for a render, so the frame kept what it had: a save could leave the owner on a stale preview with no way to refresh it but reloading the page — the thing this ticket exists to remove. Found by the browser case, invisible to every PHP test.

⚠ **AND THE BROWSER CASE COST SEVEN RUNS, SIX OF THEM THE TEST'S OWN FAULT.** Recorded because the pattern is the lesson: an oracle that could not tell the two arrangements apart (`innerText` is identical when only ORDER changes); a helper that read `/studio/preview` to get *"the stored draft"* when that route now PREFERS the unsaved key, making the assertion unsatisfiable by construction; row indices broken by a fixture shared across the whole e2e run; a save refused for a required field the case never filled; a precondition that asserted *"the preview is big enough"* and so could not explain itself; and a refusal check that matched the SUCCESS toast. **The cause was found by instrumenting — dumping the rows, the browser's own errors, and a direct GET beside the frame — and should have been instrumented after the second identical failure rather than the seventh.**

### `QRPAGER-46` — **rail, ember and tile as real templates, renderer only** — IN FLIGHT 2026-11-11 on `qrpager-46/templates`, branched off `375d14d`

> **THE `§6` PRE-CODING ANSWERS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST LINE OF CODE.** `§6.1` requires this file to change first when the data contract does, and it does: `docs/contracts/landing-page.schema.json`'s `enum` for `template` is GENERATED from `LandingTemplate::values()`, so three new cases change a committed contract artefact.

**STATED INVARIANT, in Muhammad's words — the bar a review may falsify:**

> For each of rail, ember and tile: the set of tokens the template references and the set the resolver emits are EQUAL — no reference with nothing behind it, no emitted property nothing reads.
>
> And: one unchanged tenant document, rendered under all three, produces three structurally different pages. Assert on structure — element counts, ordering, which regions exist — never on pixels.

| `§6` question | answer, before coding |
| --- | --- |
| **1. tables / columns / roles / GUCs** | **NONE.** `template` is a member of `landing_pages.draft_document` / `published_document` (`jsonb`), validated by `LandingSchema`, not a column — `§4b` B6 traced it and `LandingTemplate`'s own docblock contrasts it with `tenant_language`, which went the other way *"precisely because it IS a column"*. No migration, and the ticket's out-of-scope table names migrations explicitly. |
| **2. shared contracts** | `LandingTemplate` gains `Rail`, `Ember`, `Tile`; `classic` and `editorial` are untouched. The enum stays the ONE source: `docs/contracts/landing-page.schema.json` is regenerated by `php artisan landing:schema-export` and byte-diffed by `bin/landing-schema-check`, the studio's control is built from `cases()`, and `label()`'s `match` is exhaustive so a case without a label does not pass PHPStan. **No change to `ThemeTokens::NAMES`** — out of scope by name, and `§4b` B5's finding is that the structural half needs nothing new. |
| **3. how tenant context reaches every query** | **IT ADDS NO QUERY.** `LandingRenderer` promises *"NO DATABASE, NO REQUEST, NO TENANT CONTEXT"* and the publish path's checksum depends on it; `template` arrives inside the document the publisher already holds. The one new read is `config('design-tokens')` — a generated, tenant-independent PHP array. |
| **4. security** | No route, no input, no new tenant-authored value. The three Blades are arrangements: `block.blade.php` stays the only place a block's content is rendered, every tenant value stays `{{ }}` and `{!! !!}` appears nowhere (D5, asserted on this file's SOURCE by `LandingXssFuzzTest`). A template name that is not a case cannot reach a view path, because `page.blade.php` includes `landing.templates.{$template->value}` and the value arrived through the enum. |
| **5. scale** | Per request: one `View::make`, and the chosen arrangement's rules only — `@if` per template, so a classic page gains **no byte**, which is `QRPAGER-33`'s invariant clause 2 and is asserted byte-for-byte against `tests/Fixtures/landing/pre-template-page.html`. Bounded by `BlockSchema::MAX_BLOCKS`, unchanged. |
| **6. failure** | Rendering is pure; there is nothing to retry. The failure that matters is a token REFERENCED and not emitted — a `var()` with no value and no fallback, which paints nothing — and that is exactly what the stated invariant's first clause makes a test rather than a hope. |
| **7. version-specific research** | Blade's `@if`/`@endif` byte behaviour is the one version-specific fact here and it is MEASURED, not assumed: `QRPAGER-33` recorded 4,626 against 4,625 for a Blade comment left on a line of its own, and 4,941 for rules put in the shared block. The new `@if` blocks are therefore written `@endif@if (...)` with no newline between them, and the fixture case is the instrument. |

⚠ **THE ONE DESIGN DECISION THE TICKET DOES NOT MAKE FOR ITSELF, AND WHY IT IS DECIDED THIS WAY.** *"Zero `var()` fallback literals"* and *"the resolver emits every token the template references"* together say the resolver must supply a DEFAULT for every token a tenant has not set — and `§4b` B1's finding is that **the contract defines no defaults at all**: `NAMES` is an allow-list of names against kinds, and a token the tenant left alone is simply ABSENT from the stored map. Today the fallback literal in the Blade IS the default, which is `R-268` (one token, two greys, live).

So the defaults come from the **generated token layer** — `apps/api/config/design-tokens.php`, emitted from `packages/tokens/src/source.ts` by the same generator as `tokens.css`, with `pnpm tokens:check` byte-diffing it. Not from a literal in PHP (which `composer guard` rule 11 and `scan-panel` both refuse, `R-260`), and not from a literal in the Blade (which is the count-of-nought this ticket exists to meet). The map is `docs/design/public/{rail,ember,tile}.html` read as the ticket says to read it — *"translate every literal into a token, never copy one"*:

| contract token | default's source in `config/design-tokens.php` | the value that reaches the page |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color.background` | `colours.light.paper` | `#FCFCFA` — rail's ground |
| `color.surface` | `colours.light.surface` | `#FFFFFF` |
| `color.text` | `colours.light.ink` | `#191C22` |
| `color.muted` | `colours.light.ink-mid` | `#6B6F7A` |
| `color.accent` | `colours.light.brand` | `#191C22` — rail's CTA is ink on paper, not a colour |
| `color.accent_text` | `colours.light.paper` | `#FCFCFA` |
| `font.heading`, `font.body` | `ThemeTokens::STACKS['system']` | `system-ui, sans-serif` — the landing page loads no font file and this ticket adds none |
| `radius.small` | `radius.control` | `4px` |
| `radius.large` | `radius.surface` | `2px` |
| `space.section` | `space[64]` | `4rem` |
| `size.heading` | `size[64]` | `4rem` |

⚠ **AND `radius.large` IS SMALLER THAN `radius.small`, WHICH IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN QUIETLY FIXED.** Rail's own geometry (`QRPAGER-36`) is two roles — **surface `2px`, control `4px`** — and in `docs/design/public/rail.html` the panels and cards carry `2px` while the buttons carry `4px`. The landing contract's two radii are named *small* and *large* and are used for controls/images and for cards respectively, so mapping each to the role it is used FOR inverts the names. The alternative is inventing a third value, which is `R-268`'s own mistake in the other direction. The owner can set either, and a `radius.surface`/`radius.control` rename is a contract change this ticket is not allowed to make.

⚠ **THE DEFAULTS ARE EMITTED FOR THE THREE NEW ARRANGEMENTS ONLY.** `classic` must reproduce `pre-template-page.html` byte for byte — a twelve-property `style` attribute where it has two would change every page published before `QRPAGER-33`, which is the invariant clause the fixture exists to hold. `editorial` is *"untouched and keeps working"* by the ticket's own words. So the resolver takes the arrangement, and `R-268`'s sixteen fallbacks are **frozen by a dated baseline, not fixed** — the ticket says so: *"Do NOT fix the pre-existing literals in the old templates … Forcing a rewrite of delivered work is `R-250`."* `R-268` therefore stays OPEN with its owner; what this ticket makes unrepresentable is a NEW fallback literal.

#### The `§11` round on `QRPAGER-46` — **18 findings: 0 Critical, 2 High, 10 Medium, 6 Low**, all dispositioned

Two reviewers, one round, each given the diff and the ticket and nothing else. **QA: 12 — 0 Critical, 2 High, 6 Medium, 4 Low. ⚠⚠ **AND THE FIX PASS FOUND THREE MORE DEFECTS IN ITSELF, WHICH IS THE PATTERN THIS TICKET KEEPS PRODUCING.**

1. **The contrast case's first version judged a focus ring against the control's OWN fill** and failed on `classic`: *"a focus ring in `--color-accent` (`#0b5fff`) drawn over `.cta`, which is `--color-accent`"*. With `outline-offset:2px` the ring is drawn OUTSIDE the border box, over whatever CONTAINS the control, so that adjacency does not exist — but it WOULD at `outline-offset:0`, and the case now says so, because the offset is the only thing keeping an accent ring off an accent button on every arrangement.
2. **That same case's extraction of the `<style>` element stopped at the `</style>` QUOTED INSIDE the element's own Blade comment** — the third appearance of this one hazard in this ticket, after the masker's two-elements-in-one-file and the `@endif@if` compile error. Comments are stripped before the element is found, which is what `maskBladeCss()` already encodes.
3. **The DOM read of `tile`'s grid was a string slice** from `<div class="tile-grid">` to the next `</div>`, which closes the block's own inner `<div class="grid">`; it failed on correct markup. A string landmark cannot find the end of a nested element — this project's third payment for that lesson.

⚠ **ONE ENVIRONMENT FACT THE QA REVIEWER MEASURED, RECORDED BECAUSE IT MAKES EVIDENCE FALSE RATHER THAN MISSING:** `php artisan test` renders a **stale compiled Blade view** after an edit to `page.blade.php` — the rendered `<style>` carried the previous edit until `php artisan view:clear`. A falsification of a template that stays green is not evidence until the compiled views are cleared, and every measurement in this record was taken with that done.

⚠ **AND THE ROUND ITSELF EXPOSED A PROCESS DEFECT, FILED AS `R-297`:** the security reviewer caught this session mutating and reverting tracked files — the recorded falsifications — WHILE the round was running, and one of its own measurements landed inside such a window and read green for the wrong reason. It re-verified every load-bearing measurement against the committed blobs and said so, which is the only reason the round's figures stand. `§11`'s own convention is detached worktrees; this session ran the reviewers in the main tree.

#### What the SCREENSHOTS found, which no test in this feature could — 2026-11-11, before merge

Muhammad, before merging: *"render the same tenant document under rail, ember and tile and give me the three, as screenshots at 1280 and at 390. I cannot switch templates from the panel until `QRPAGER-47`, and I am not building the picker on top of three templates I have never seen."*

Twelve captures: three arrangements × two widths × **two theme states** — the fixture tenant's own stored theme (a blue accent, a white ground, a serif heading), and **no theme at all**, which is what `QRPAGER-46` is actually for (*"a client gets a DESIGNED page instead of a blank one"*) and where every one of the twelve tokens comes from `ThemeDefaults`. One unchanged document, six photographs, rendered to files and captured full-page from `file://` — the renderer promises no database and no request, so the bytes on disk ARE what a visitor receives.

**TWO DEFECTS, BOTH OF THIS TICKET'S OWN MAKING, BOTH INVISIBLE TO EVERY TEST IT WROTE.**

1. **A heading as large as the page title, in all three arrangements.** The shared rule is `h1,section:first-of-type h2{font-size:var(--size-heading)}`, written when every block was a direct child of `main` — so *"the first section"* meant THE HERO. Each new arrangement puts blocks in a wrapper of its own and `:first-of-type` is scoped to the PARENT, so the rule started matching whatever happened to be first inside it: `ember` rendered *"How the pager works"* at 64px, `tile` *"The room"*, `rail` *"Find us"* — each the same size as the real title above it. Fixed with one `font-size:revert` per wrapper, which is *"whatever the other `h2`s get"* and needs no token.
2. **`rail` was a column of five enormous photographs.** `display:block` on the shared `.grid` is what makes the arrangement a column, and it also makes every image full-measure: **6,618px tall against `tile`'s 2,777**, with the ledger lost between them — a restaurant with a dozen dishes would publish twenty thousand pixels of photograph. Fixed with `aspect-ratio:16/5;object-fit:cover` on that arrangement's grid images, a RATIO rather than a magnitude. The page is 4,324px now and reads as the reference artboard does.

⚠⚠⚠ **SAID PLAINLY, BECAUSE IT IS THE MOST USEFUL SENTENCE IN THIS RECORD: THE ONLY CONTROL THAT CAUGHT EITHER DEFECT WAS A HUMAN LOOKING AT A RENDER.**

Not a test, not a gate, not a review round — all three had already passed on both. Eighteen `§11` findings were dispositioned, four gates were green, and two defects were visible in the first screenshot anybody took. The reason is exact and worth keeping:

- **Both were COMPUTED values** — a font size and a document height — and the ticket's stated invariant says *"assert on structure — element counts, ordering, which regions exist — **never on pixels**"*. The structural tests were **right and blind at the same time**: the right heading in the right region, in the right order, every block rendered exactly once. Nothing they are allowed to look at was wrong.
- **The `e2e` suite has no subject here either.** `browser/studio.spec.ts`'s document names no template, so every preview the journey suite renders is `classic`. The three arrangements have never been in a browser against a real stack — `R-303`, recorded against `QRPAGER-47` so it is inherited rather than rediscovered.

⚠⚠ **AND CI REFUSED THAT CONTROL THREE TIMES, EVERY TIME FOR A REAL REASON — the instrument needed the same scrutiny as the code it measures, and got it from CI rather than from here. All three are ONE SHAPE: a step that is only correct on a machine somebody already configured.**

1. **The spec hard-coded `/repo/storage/landing-preview`**, which is the path INSIDE the browsers container. This host runs the engines in that container; CI runs them natively, where the repository is at `/home/runner/work/qr-pager/qr-pager` — so all thirteen cases failed there with *"is not there"* while passing here. A path correct on one of the two machines the gate runs on is exactly the defect `tools/browsers/bin/browsers` exists to remove. Resolved from `import.meta.url` now.
2. **The journey suite collected the new project.** `tools/browsers/bin/e2e` runs `playwright test` with **no project filter** — the journey suite is *everything that is not the kit* — so the `Pint, PHPStan, Pest` job went red on thirteen cases whose pages only `gate:templates` renders. Playwright has no exclude-a-project flag and listing the journey's fourteen projects in that script would be a second list to keep in step, so the project is **declared only when `QRPAGER_TEMPLATE_GATE=1`**; `browsers` forwards every `QRPAGER_*` variable by pattern, so that works natively and in the container. `lint-scope.test.mjs` now asserts BOTH states — absent by default, present when the gate asks — which is CI's finding turned into a test.
3. **The fresh clone had no environment file, so the instrument refused to run.** `gate:templates` boots `apps/api`; a clone has no `.env`; Laravel's default for an unset `APP_ENV` is `production`; and the instrument fails closed — *“render-arrangements is a development instrument and refuses to run as production.”* ⚠ **AND THE SAME RUNNER RAN THE SAME GATE TWICE AND GOT TWO ANSWERS:** CI's own `gate:templates` step carried `cp apps/api/.env.example apps/api/.env` and `key:generate` and was GREEN, while `tools/gate/bin/fresh-clone-proof`'s clone, three steps later in the same job, was RED on that step — runs `43114380476` and `43114388980` at `0d02d25`. The clone script now runs the two lines `CLAUDE.md` gives a fresh clone and `apps/api/bin/fresh-clone-proof` already ran. ⚠ **THE GUARD IS LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY:** a gate that exported `APP_ENV=local` to get past it would be a guard any caller can switch off, and a fail-closed guard that every caller disarms is worse than none. `ci-parity.test.mjs` DERIVES the requirement instead of naming this step — any gate step whose `package.json` script shells to `php` or `artisan` obliges the clone to bootstrap an environment — so the next one is covered the day it is added; proven red with the `cp` line removed.

⚠ **SO THE CONTROL IS NOW REPEATABLE RATHER THAN LEFT TO WHOEVER REMEMBERS TO LOOK** — Muhammad's instruction of 2026-11-11. `tools/landing/render-arrangements.php` renders one document under every arrangement; `browser/landing-templates.spec.ts`, in a project of its own, measures the two computed values and captures the twelve photographs; `pnpm run gate:templates` is both halves in order; and `bin/gate`'s step list and CI's frontend job both carry that one command, with `ci-parity.test.mjs` holding the two in step (its exact-count guard on playwright-launching scripts went from one to two, named rather than widened). ⚠ **AND THE INSTRUMENT IS A TOOL RATHER THAN AN ARTISAN COMMAND BECAUSE `composer deptrac` REFUSED THE COMMAND:** *"App\Features\Landing\Console\RenderArrangementsCommand must not depend on Tests\Support\LandingFixtures"*, three violations. The rule is right, and the dependency is deliberate — the document this renders IS the test fixture, because a second sample document would be a second source for *"the document"*. So it sits in `tools/`, outside the layers deptrac governs, in `bin/fresh-clone-proof`'s posture: a development instrument that boots the application rather than being part of it, and refuses to run outside local/testing. `composer stan` had already refused the first version for five real GD type errors, one of which was an unchecked `false` from `imagecolorallocate`; those checks came with it. The two assertions are **exactly the class that bit**, and each was shown RED on the code this ticket shipped an hour earlier:

| the assertion | red on what shipped |
| --- | --- |
| exactly ONE visible heading computes at the page's largest size, in every arrangement and both theme states | *"rail shows more than one heading at the page's largest size (64px)"* — and the same for `ember` and `tile`, 12 cases red |
| the document's height stays under a bound stated for this fixture — 5,000px at 1280, 5,500 at 390 | *"rail at 1280 renders 6618px for a document of seven blocks and six photographs"* |

The heading rule is *"exactly one"* rather than *"no section heading matches the title"*, because in `classic` the page's own `h1` is visually hidden and the hero's `h2` IS the display heading — a rule about the `h1` would fail on a page that is right. What was wrong is that a SECOND visible heading joined it. The height bound is stated for ONE document — seven blocks, six photographs — and sits between the tallest correct arrangement (4,324px) and the defect (6,618px), which is the only honest way to write a bound on a magnitude.

The captures are at `storage/landing-preview/{default,tenant}-{rail,ember,tile}-{1280,390}.png`, regenerated by `storage/landing-preview/render.php` and `shoot.mjs` (git-ignored: instruments, not deliverables).

| what | whose code | why it was fixed here anyway |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SupportPanelActionTest`'s tenant slug was a 20-hex uuid7 PREFIX, which collides inside one millisecond | Task 6's support panel, delivered long before this ticket | It reddened a FULL-SUITE run at HEAD with `23505 tenants_slug_unique` and passed alone, so `§6`'s *"all previous tasks' tests still pass"* could not be discharged deterministically while it stood. The reason is written ten lines below it in its own file, for the sibling slug |
| `OpenApiSpecTest`'s implicit 60-second `Process` deadline | Task 4's OpenAPI surface | It reddened `bin/fresh-clone-proof`, which is `§6`'s *"the gates pass from a fresh clone"*. `R-301` files the class: `Illuminate\Process`'s default applies to every `Process::run()` in the suite and nothing says which of them chose it |
| the same case discarding its process result, so three FAILED exports would hash equal and pass as *"deterministic"* | the same | Found while fixing the deadline. **Folded into `R-290`** on Muhammad's instruction rather than left loose: a test that cannot fail is that row's whole subject, and *"a check built on comparing several runs is vacuous unless each run is asserted to have succeeded"* is the class |
| `ArchitectureGuardTest`'s deptrac run, under the same implicit 60-second deadline | Task 8b's architecture guard | **A FOURTH, and it is the same class as the second** — `R-301` predicted it in as many words (*"the default applies to every `Process::run()` in this suite"*) and the next clone run demonstrated it. deptrac over 471 files with no cache is a minute idle and several under load. Fixed because it blocked the same `§6` clause; the other **ten** call sites with no deadline are the sweep and stay with `R-301`'s owner |

⚠ **AND THE BOUNDARY IS NOT DISSOLVED BY THIS.** A fence keeps a ticket from growing; it does not license shipping a gate that does not pass. What distinguishes these three from scope creep is that each was found BY a `§6` gate refusing this ticket's own tree, and each is one line plus its reasoning — none of them changes a behaviour, a contract or a surface. Anything that did would have been a stop-and-report.

⚠ **TWO LOSSES AGAINST THE ARTBOARDS, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN.**

1. **`ember`'s band is a panel inside the measure, not full-bleed.** Breaking out of `main`'s padding needs that padding's own value — the literal `1rem` in the shared rules, frozen by the baseline and not a token — and `margin-inline:calc(50% - 50vw)` carries a magnitude the scanner refuses. Inventing a fourth spacing literal would be `R-268` with this ticket's name on it.
2. **The three share ONE palette: the tenant's, or the Rail defaults.** `docs/design/public/ember.html` is a warm near-black artboard and `tile.html` a teal one, and **not one of those values is in the token layer**. The ticket's own rule for those files is *"REFERENCE ONLY: translate every literal into a token, never copy one"*, and `ThemeTokens::NAMES` may not grow here — so *"structure, not palette, is what separates them"* is both the ticket's instruction and the only thing the contract can express. `ember` reads as dark by SWAPPING the tenant's own two colours, which is the one translation available.

⚠ **AND A CONSEQUENCE THAT IS NOT A PANEL CHANGE BUT LOOKS LIKE ONE:** the studio's arrangement control is built from `LandingTemplate::cases()`, so it now offers **five** options with no panel code touched. That is what makes the three reachable at all; the panel UI work — a preview of each, a better control — is `QRPAGER-47` and nothing here anticipates it.

### `QRPAGER-47` — **the theme tab: three themes, a logo, colour pickers, fonts** — IN FLIGHT 2026-11-12 on `qrpager-47/theme-tab`, branched off `2892954`

> **THE `§6` PRE-CODING ANSWERS, WRITTEN BEFORE THE FIRST LINE OF CODE.** `§6.1` requires this file to change first when the data contract does, and this ticket changes it in **three** places: `LandingTemplate` loses two cases, `LandingDocument::KEYS` gains `logo`, and `ThemeTokens::STACKS` gains the Arabic font choice. ⚠ **AND IT CARRIES THE PROJECT'S FIRST DATA MIGRATION**, which `PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md §4 › Postgres traps` says *"blocks the first data migration anyone writes"* — the pattern is settled in `§2.10` and is followed here rather than re-derived.

**STATED INVARIANT, in Muhammad's words — the bar a review may falsify:**

> After the migration, no stored document references a retired case — proven by a test that fails if any does, across every tenant.
>
> And: choosing a theme in the picker is reflected in the preview with no Save click and no page refresh.

| `§6` question | answer, before coding |
| --- | --- |
| **1. tables / columns / roles / GUCs** | **ROWS, for the first time in this project — and no column, type or constraint.** `landing_pages.draft_document` and `landing_pages.published_document`, both `jsonb` (`§4b` B2), where `template` is a MEMBER and not a column. **Both columns, not just the draft:** `MediaLibrary` already treats the pair as one population when it counts references (`MediaLibrary.php:167`), a `published_document` naming a retired case would fail `LandingDocument::fromInput()` the next time it is read, and the stated invariant says *"no stored document"*. **Roles:** the migration runs as `qrpager_owner` (`php artisan migrate --database=pgsql_owner`) — never as `app`. **GUCs:** `app.tenant_id` per tenant, and `app.bypass_tenant` for ONE statement only (see 3). |
| **2. shared contracts** | **`LandingTemplate` drops `Classic` and `Editorial`** — five cases become three — and **`DEFAULT` moves from `Classic` to `Rail`**, which is what makes a document with no `template` member render as the ledger without a write. **`LandingDocument::KEYS` gains `logo`**, and **not `REQUIRED`**, for the reason `template` is absent from it: every document stored before today carries no such member and a required one would invalidate all of them at once. ~~**`ThemeTokens::STACKS` gains the Arabic choice**~~ — ⚠ **CANCELLED BY RULING 2 OF 2026-11-12: `STACKS` is UNCHANGED by this ticket.** The font section is deferred whole (`R-306`), so no stack was added and no contract member moved for it. Each stays a single source: `docs/contracts/landing-page.schema.json` is regenerated by `php artisan landing:schema-export` and byte-diffed by `bin/landing-schema-check`, the studio's controls are built from `cases()`, and `composer guard` rule 11c parses `ThemeTokens` rather than holding a copy. |
| **3. how tenant context reaches every query** | **`§2.10` pattern 1, which is the preferred one and is already proven by `DataMigrationPatternTest`.** The ONE thing the owner cannot do under FORCE RLS is enumerate tenants — `tenants` carries `tenant_isolation_tenants` and the owner is bound by it — so that single read runs inside `withoutTenantScope('2026_11_12 QRPAGER-47 retire classic and editorial: list tenants', …)`, which refuses on any role but `qrpager_owner`, refuses inside a tenant scope, and writes its own `audit_log` row (`actor_type = system`, `action = tenancy.bypass`) inside the same transaction. Every write is then `withTenant($id, …, 'pgsql_owner')`. ⚠ **AND EVERY STATEMENT IS KEYED:** `UPDATE landing_pages SET … WHERE id = ? AND draft_document->>'template' = 'classic'`, with the affected-row count read back. `§4 › Postgres traps` is explicit that a bulk statement referencing no column of the table **escapes RLS row filtering entirely** and writes rows the role cannot read — *"a data migration running as `owner` under FORCE RLS is the most likely place this bites."* There is one row per tenant (`landing_pages_tenant_unique`), so the loop is one keyed statement per column per tenant and the count is 0 or 1, never more. ⚠ **THE PANEL ADDS ONE READ PER FORM BUILD, AND THIS ROW CLAIMED NONE** — `§11` QA round, Low 4. `ThemePage::form()` calls `LandingPages::draft()` for the badge, which is a full `withTenant` scope (`§2.11`: about four statements, two round trips) on every Livewire update of this page — including the ones the preview's 400ms debounce fires. It is the same shape `MediaOptions` already has on this tab and the badge cannot be answered without it: the arrangement the DRAFT names is the only honest meaning of *in use now*. Named rather than removed, because the alternative is a badge that follows the click. |
| **4. security** | **No new route, no new entry point.** The logo is **a choice from the tenant's own media library** — the `Select` + `MediaOptions` path `seo_og_image` already uses — and explicitly **NOT** Filament's `FileUpload`, which writes bytes to the object store without passing `InspectedImage` and would remove a Task 7 control (the ticket names this). The chosen value is a media-asset **id**, validated against that tenant's own assets, so it carries no path and no bytes. Colours stay `ThemeTokens::accepts()`'s lower-case hex — not `rgb()`, not `color-mix()`, not `var()` — and a font is a **key of `STACKS`**, never a stack the tenant writes. The migration opens the one bypass this project has, for one `SELECT` of ids, audited. |
| **5. scale** | **The migration is O(tenants)**, two keyed statements each, one transaction per tenant, no table scan and no bulk statement. **Per published page:** one `<img>` for the logo when one is set, and **no new network request for fonts** — ⚠ **AND THE REASON IS NOW RULING 2 RATHER THAN THIS SENTENCE: nothing about fonts shipped at all.** What this said was that *both families are self-hosted and subset in* `packages/tokens/fonts`, which is true of **Tajawal and Archivo only** — Cairo is not in the repository, which is half of why item 4 was deferred. The panel's own faces are self-hosted, which `§12`'s cold-3G clause and `source.ts`'s own note require (*"a third-party font request … discloses their IP to that third party"*). **Per panel render:** three thumbnails, each inline SVG built from tokens, so no asset request and nothing to cache. |
| **6. failure** | **Idempotent by construction:** the `WHERE` names the value being replaced, so a second run matches nothing and reports 0 rows. ⚠⚠ **PARTIAL FAILURE IS ALL-OR-NOTHING, AND THIS ROW SAID THE OPPOSITE UNTIL THE `§11` QA ROUND READ IT AGAINST `§2.10`.** It claimed *"`withTenant` runs each tenant's work in its own transaction, so a failure leaves earlier tenants migrated and later ones untouched"*. **False, and this file already said why 7,000 lines earlier:** `§2.10` records that `Migrator` wraps every migration in a transaction because `PostgresGrammar` reports `supportsSchemaTransactions`, so *"a migration body is already at transaction level 1"* and each `withTenant` opens a SAVEPOINT inside it. A failure at tenant nine rolls back tenants one through eight with it. ⚠ **THE REAL BEHAVIOUR IS SAFER THAN THE CLAIM**, which is why no test caught it: there is no half-migrated state to recover from, and re-running after a repair starts clean. What the claim would have made a reader do — trust that a second run finishes a partial job — is now unnecessary rather than wrong. ⚠ **AND `down()` IS A DELIBERATE NO-OP, WHICH IS A DESIGN DECISION AND NOT AN OMISSION:** `up()` writes only `rail` and `ember`, and **both cases exist in the rolled-back code as well** — the retirement removes `classic` and `editorial`, it does not remove the two the data now names. So a rollback leaves every stored document valid against the restored enum, and a `down()` that mapped `rail → classic` could not tell a tenant who was migrated from one who CHOSE the ledger, and would silently rewrite the second one's page. `§6`'s *"a rollback of this task's migrations runs clean"* is proven by running it, and by re-applying `up()` afterwards. |
| **7. version-specific research** | `jsonb_set(document, '{template}', '"rail"'::jsonb, false)` with **`create_missing = false`**, so a document that carries no `template` member is **not written** — it inherits the new `DEFAULT` instead, and the migration touches only rows that explicitly name a retired case. Verified by running it against this project's Postgres 16 rather than assumed, and `jsonb_set` is used in place of decode-change-encode in PHP so that no document is re-serialised: a round trip through `json_encode` would rewrite key order and whitespace on every tenant's page and make the migration's diff unbounded. |

#### PART A — what the retirement and the first data migration actually did

| part | where |
| --- | --- |
| two cases retired, `DEFAULT` moved `Classic → Rail` | `app/Domain/Landing/LandingTemplate.php` — and `docs/contracts/landing-page.schema.json`'s `enum` regenerated by `php artisan landing:schema-export` |
| the data migration | `database/migrations/2026_11_12_120000_retire_classic_and_editorial.php` |
| the stated invariant, and the sweep that proves it bites | `tests/Feature/Landing/RetiredTemplateTest.php` — 6 cases |
| the two Blade files deleted, the `editorial` branch removed from the rule chain | `resources/views/landing/templates/{classic,editorial}.blade.php`, `resources/views/landing/page.blade.php` |
| `resolvesEveryToken()` deleted — every remaining arrangement answers true | `app/Features/Landing/ThemeStylesheet.php` now asks *"is there an arrangement at all"* |
| the frozen-literal baseline pruned, by the scanner's own findings | `tools/design-tokens/landing-baseline.json` — 32 entries → **27**, 34 literals still frozen |

⚠ **THE MIGRATION TOUCHES BOTH DOCUMENT COLUMNS, AND THE REASON IS NOT SYMMETRY.** A
`published_document` naming a retired case is refused by `LandingDocument::fromStored()` exactly
like a draft — `fromStored()` routes through `fromInput()` by design — so the media library's
reference sweep and the next republish would both fail for that tenant. `MediaLibrary` already
treats the pair as one population (`MediaLibrary.php:167`), and the stated invariant says *"no
stored document"*.

⚠⚠ **WHAT THE MIGRATION DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO: RE-PUBLISH.** `published_checksum` is
`hash('sha256', $html)` over the bytes the publisher wrote, and `{checksum}.html` on the object
store is immutable. Rewriting the stored `published_document` does **not** re-render those bytes,
so after this migration a tenant who was on `classic` has: a stored published document naming
`rail`, and a live page on the CDN still rendered as `classic` — until their next publish. That is
the honest state and it is the right one: a migration that re-rendered and re-uploaded every
tenant's page would be a publish run inside a schema migration, with the object store, the
manifest and the pointer in play and no way to roll any of it back. **Recorded as `R-304`**, owner
`QRPAGER-47`, so the next publish being the repair is a decision on the record rather than a
surprise.

⚠ **AND THE ONE THING THE RETIREMENT COSTS, NAMED RATHER THAN DROPPED QUIETLY.** `classic` was
the arrangement that reproduced `tests/Fixtures/landing/pre-template-page.html` **byte for byte** —
`QRPAGER-33`'s invariant clause 2, *"a tenant who published yesterday and republishes today gets the
same page"*, and a capture that could not have been taken after the fact. Retiring the case retires
the guarantee: those tenants' pages CHANGE on their next publish. That is the ticket's intent — the
complaint being answered is that the old pair was indistinguishable — so the CASE is retired with it.
⚠ **THE FIXTURE FILE ITSELF IS KEPT AND IS NO LONGER ASSERTED BY ANYTHING**, which is a deliberate pair of
decisions rather than an oversight: it is a capture of the published page as it stood on 2026-11-03 and
cannot be re-taken, so deleting it would destroy the only record of what those tenants were being served —
and holding new work to it would be holding the product to an arrangement it no longer has. What replaces the case
asserts the half that is still load-bearing: **a document naming no arrangement renders identically
to one naming `rail` explicitly**, which is what makes the migration's `create_missing => false`
safe for every pre-`QRPAGER-33` document.

| the six cases, and what each would catch | |
| --- | --- |
| both cases gone from the enum, `values()` is `rail, ember, tile`, `DEFAULT` is `Rail` | the premise every other case rests on — a rename rather than a retirement would leave them all vacuous |
| **no stored document names a retired case, across every tenant** | the stated invariant, swept through `withoutTenantScope()` — the one cross-tenant mechanism — over BOTH columns, with the planted state asserted first so the case cannot pass on an empty premise |
| a document planted AFTER the migration IS reported | Muhammad's standing instruction of 2026-11-03: every new proof is shown to redden once. An empty sweep contains no `classic` either |
| a second run writes nothing; a tenant on `tile` is byte-identical | idempotency and the keyed form in one case — `migrateColumn()` throws on any count but 1, so a re-run that matched its own output would raise rather than pass quietly |
| **exactly ONE audited bypass**, counted by its own reason | `§2.10` pattern 1 rather than pattern 2: a bypass per tenant would migrate correctly, be audited, and have widened the one path this project keeps narrow |
| `migrate:rollback` then `migrate`, both exit 0, data unchanged | `§6`'s rollback clause — the only thing that makes a deliberate no-op `down()` an honest decision rather than an omission |

⚠⚠ **FIVE THINGS THIS TICKET'S OWN PROOFS FOUND IN ITS OWN CODE, every one of them by a gate
rather than by reading.** ⚠ **IT SAID FOUR UNTIL 2026-11-12**, and the fifth was found by the
scoped `§11` pass on `0e72316` (QA L-1) — an enumeration that is short by one is the shape
`R-300` records, so it is corrected here rather than left to read as complete:

1. **`hiddenLabel()` PUT ENGLISH IN AN ARABIC PANEL, INVISIBLY.** `Filament\Forms\Components\Field::getLabel()` falls back to a label DERIVED from the field name whenever none is `filled()` — and `->label('')` does not stop it, because `''` is not `filled()` either. So nine fields rendered `fi-sr-only` labels reading *Template*, *Logo*, *Theme color background*, *Theme color surface*… — invisible, and read aloud to exactly the reader who cannot see the row's real name. `StudioLocalizationTest` caught it by rendering every tab under `ar` and reading the text nodes. Fixed by overriding `getDefaultLabel()` to return `''` on all three custom fields, which makes the wrapper emit no label element at all.
2. **A DEAD `match` ARM, REFUSED BY PHPSTAN, AND THE SAFETY IT WAS REACHING FOR SURVIVED ANYWAY.** `StudioForm::theme()` skips colours with a `continue` and then kept a `ThemeTokenKind::Colour` arm *"so a new kind fails to compile here"*; `match.alwaysFalse` refused it, because the narrowed type after the `continue` is `FontChoice|Length`. Removing the arm keeps the property: a new kind widens that type, the match stops being exhaustive, and the analysis fails on the same line.
3. **A CAST PHPSTAN WAS RIGHT TO REFUSE.** `ColourField` named its row from `(string) $this->getLabel()` as a fallback — `Htmlable|string|null`. The refusal pointed at a real defect rather than a type nicety: with `getDefaultLabel()` now returning `''`, that fallback could only ever have produced an empty name while reading as though it had one.
4. **A NEW SPACING LITERAL IN THE LANDING PAGE, CAUGHT BY THE SCANNER THE PREVIOUS TICKET BUILT.** The logo's own rule was written `padding:var(--space-section) 1rem 0`, and `scan-css` refused the `1rem` with no baseline entry to hide behind (`R-267`'s machinery, one ticket old, working on its author). The fix is better than the literal: `main,.mark{…}` gives the mark the page's own measure and gutter, so there is one gutter rather than two.
5. **TWO MEASURED HEXES IN A COMMENT, REFUSED BY THE PANEL SCANNER — THE `no-raw-color` FAMILY'S THIRD APPEARANCE IN THIS REPOSITORY AND ITS SECOND IN THIS VERY FILE.** `ColourField`'s docblock recorded what the `§11` QA round measured for the contrast-direction fix by QUOTING the pair, and `pnpm lint:panel` refused both: *“a hex in panel PHP is a design decision taken outside the token layer whether or not anything paints with it”*. Fixed in `0e72316` by describing the operands and keeping the ratio. ⚠ **THE SCANNER WAS RIGHT AND THE FIX IS THE WEAKER FORM**, which the same scoped pass said in its own Medium — `R-316`.

⚠⚠ **TWO OPEN ITEMS, NAMED HERE BEFORE THEY ARE DISCOVERED LATE. NEITHER BLOCKS PART A.**

1. ~~**THE ARTBOARD IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY.**~~ ⚠ **SUPERSEDED 2026-11-12: Muhammad added `docs/design/studio/theme-tab.html` and it is committed with this ticket** (`43431fe`, the same commit as the components — `§12` wants the direction approved BEFORE any component is written, and this record is the only thing that can carry that ordering: the board was approved and read first, the commit is one). The item is kept rather than deleted because it is what was true when Part A shipped, and because the answer to it is a ruling.
