So the Cairo half of *"Tajawal and Cairo"* cannot be shipped by naming it: the subset `.woff2` has to exist first. Shipping the option without the file would give an owner who picks Cairo a page rendered in something else, which is the defect `§12`'s single-source rule is written against.

#### PART C — `R-303` DISCHARGED, AND THE RECORD REPAIRED (2026-11-12, after the `§11` round)

> **Muhammad's ruling, verbatim, when this session proposed re-dispositioning `R-303`:** *"grow
> the case. Do not re-disposition it. Its proof names two halves and only one exists: the picker
> reaching the PREVIEW. The published page is the half that matters, because the preview is a
> panel surface and the customer never sees it … Re-filing a row owned by this ticket, from
> inside this ticket, because its test is incomplete, is how `§5` reached 314."*

⚠⚠ **THE GAP WAS BIGGER THAN A CASE, AND THAT IS THE FINDING.** `R-303`'s proof asks for *"a
published page whose served CSS carries that arrangement's marker and no other's"* — and
**nothing in `gate:e2e` served a public page at all.** Measured rather than assumed: `apps/api`
has no landing route (`routes/` holds none), `TemplateArrangementTest` calls
`LandingRenderer::render()` directly, `browser/landing-templates.spec.ts` renders from the
FILESYSTEM, and the arrangement case at `studio.spec.ts` asserts the panel's PREVIEW pane. The
serving layer is `apps/site`, a separate Next.js process that reads the object store by `Host`,
and **it had never been started by the e2e harness.** So the three arrangements had no
end-to-end subject because the surface they are served on was not in the suite.

| part | where |
| --- | --- |
| `apps/site` built, started and waited on, inside the e2e stack | `tools/browsers/bin/e2e` — the production build (never the dev server), `PORT` rather than `-- --port`, `setsid` so the group reaches `next-server`: **`tools/gate/bin/site-isolation-proof`'s recipe, including the parts it learned the hard way** |
| the catch-all route proven **dynamic** from the build log | a prerendered answer here is one host's page served to every host — Task 11's whole invariant |
| readiness checked WITHOUT `-f` | a bare origin carries no tenant host, so 404 is the designed answer and still proves the process is serving; `-f` would spin to the timeout against a healthy server |
| the one new environment contract | `QRPAGER_E2E_SITE_BASE` |
| the case itself | `browser/studio.spec.ts` — *serves the arrangement the picker chose, and no other, on the PUBLISHED page* |

⚠ **IT IS A SIBLING CASE RATHER THAN A GROWTH OF THE EXISTING ONE, FOR TWO REASONS, BOTH
MEASURED.** The case above it is titled *reflects an arrangement change with **no Save** and no
refresh* and asserts that the stored draft does **not** move — a publish is a save followed by a
render, so adding one would have falsified that case's own premise. And this file's own docblock
records that an earlier shape *"grew a published-bytes assertion"* and then **exceeded the
90-second budget**, which is the second reason the published half belongs in a case with its own.

⚠⚠ **THE FIRST VERSION OF THE HARNESS SEEDED SHARED STATE TO LEARN ONE STRING, AND THE SUITE
CAUGHT IT ON RUN ONE.** It called `bin/publish-landing-fixture` for alpha so the case could read
the hostname out of a file — and that script goes through `saveDraft()`, which **overwrites the
restaurant's draft document**. The studio specs drive that same draft. Measured: **546 passed, 3
failed** — `studio.spec.ts:1047` (a label locator resolving to **16** elements), `:1590` (a block
that would not add: `toHaveCount` expected 3, received 2) and `:2045` — **and the new case itself
PASSED.** A harness that seeds fixture state to learn one string pays for it in every case that
reads that state.

⚠ **SO THE HOSTNAME COMES OFF THE PRODUCT, WHICH IS ALSO THE BETTER PROVENANCE.**
`builder.blade.php` renders `$state['hostname']` — `hostnameInScope()`, which prefers an active
custom domain over the platform one — through `studio.partials.emphasised`, which emits the value
in a `<strong>` **because `{!! !!}` is refused in this application** (`RepoGuardTest`). So the one
`<strong>` on the status plate IS the host the page will be served on, stated by the panel rather
than derived in a spec — which is what `apps/site`'s own docblock asks for when it says the
hostname rule is *imported, never restated*. Nothing is published before the suite now.

The case picks **the arrangement that is NOT stored** (`(stored + 1) % 3`), because publishing the
one the tenant already had would assert the marker of a page that was already being served, and
would pass against a picker that wrote nothing.

⚠⚠ **THE REDDEN PROOF FOUND A DEFECT THE GREEN RUN COULD NOT — AND IT WAS NOT THE ONE IT WENT
LOOKING FOR.** Muhammad's standing instruction of 2026-11-03 is that every new proof is shown to
redden once. Run with `-g` **in isolation**, the case did not fail at its marker: it timed out at
`page.waitForResponse` waiting 30 s for the publish POST. Playwright's own page dump says why —
the status plate read `studio.page.empty`, *“لا توجد كتل في صفحتك بعد”* — so **Publish was
disabled and the click did nothing.** The case had been passing in the full suite **only because
earlier cases had left blocks behind.** An ordering dependency is precisely what `R-303`'s proof
must not have: the whole point of the row is that the published page has no subject of its own,
and a case that borrows another case's state has not given it one. It now **adds its own block and
saves** before it publishes.

⚠ **AND A SECOND ORDER-DEPENDENCE WAS CLOSED BEFORE IT COULD BITE.** `findIndex` returns `-1`
when the document names no arrangement — which is not *"none is in effect"*: a document with no
`template` member renders as `LandingTemplate::DEFAULT`, which Part A moved to `rail`. Picking
`(-1 + 1) % 3 = 0` would, on a tenant that has never chosen, publish `rail` over a page already
rendering as `rail` and assert a marker that was there before the case ran. The index is now taken
from the **effective** arrangement, so *"not stored"* means *"not the one in effect"*.

| the three runs, and what each establishes | result |
| --- | --- |
| the case **in isolation**, before the fix | **RED at `page.waitForResponse`** — 30 s, publish disabled on an empty page. The ordering dependency, found |
| the case **in isolation**, after the fix (**run A**) | **1 passed (3.6s), green** — it stands on its own |
| the case **in isolation** with the marker map **rotated**, so each arrangement expects another's (**run B**) | **RED at `studio.spec.ts:2042`** — `expect.poll(servedHtml).toContain(markers[chosen])`, the SERVED-page assertion. **Not vacuous: it is bound to the arrangement the picker chose** |

⚠ **THE ROTATION IS THE RIGHT FALSIFICATION AND A PLANTED FAILURE WOULD NOT HAVE BEEN.** `R-303`
asks for *"a journey case that fails when the picker writes the wrong `template`"*. Rotating the
map makes the case expect the marker of an arrangement the picker did **not** choose — which is
what *the wrong template reached the page* looks like from the served bytes, and it is the one
assertion that could have been passing for free.

The only advice case drives `#c9c48f` against a near-white default, so `mine < theirs` and the DARKEN arm runs; inverting the ternary at `StudioPanelProvider.php:498` leaves every suite green | ✅ **FIXED, with a regression test shown to redden.** Muhammad's ruling of 2026-11-12: *“A High blocks the tag — `§11`, and the fix-diff cap has not been reached. `R-315`'s line was written for a Low and does not reach up.”* And on the substance: `adviceLighten` *“is what an owner reads at the moment their colour is unreadable, and `§12` requires that message say what to do … dark text on a dark ground is the most common mistake there is”* |

| **L-2** | Low | *“`R-260` for the third time”* is loose: that row is *“a source commit was pushed without running the gate”*, and nothing was pushed red — `886e532` was never a remote tip | **`R-317`**, owner `QRPAGER-34` |

| 11 | `space.section` | 59 | Length | Space between sections · المسافة بين الأقسام |
| 12 | `size.heading` | 60 | Length | Heading size · حجم العناوين |

⚠ **THE QUESTION ASKED FOR EACH ONE'S CURRENT VALUE, AND THERE IS NO SUCH THING — THAT IS THE FINDING, NOT A GAP IN THE AUDIT.** `NAMES` is an allow-list of names against kinds; it carries no defaults and the contract defines none. A token the tenant has not set is **absent from the stored map**, and absent means *use the arrangement's own value* — `StudioForm::toDocument()` keeps a member only when it is a non-empty string. The only values the contract does hold are the four font STACKS at `ThemeTokens.php:73-76`: `system`, `sans`, `serif`, `mono`.

### B2 — where a tenant's theme is stored

**Table** `landing_pages`, **columns** `draft_document` and `published_document`, **type `jsonb`** — `apps/api/database/migrations/2026_10_28_160000_create_landing_tables.php:50` and `:53`. One row per tenant, enforced by `landing_pages_tenant_unique` at `:62`, which is what makes *"the tenant's page"* an object with no selection step anywhere.

The theme is **one member of that document**, not a column. Top-level keys measured on a seeded tenant: `["seo", "theme", "blocks", "template"]`. The theme member is a **flat map of dotted name → string, carrying only what was overridden**. One real stored value, read from the seeded tenant `01a1c28c-…`:

```json
{"color.accent":"#da6110","color.background":"#eee8e8"}
```

Two of twelve present; the other ten are not empty strings, they are **absent**.

### B3 — what the public renderer reads, traced

| step | file:line | what happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| stored | `database/migrations/2026_10_28_160000_create_landing_tables.php:50` | `draft_document` / `published_document` jsonb |
| validated | `app/Domain/Landing/LandingDocument.php` | the `theme` member is refused unless every name is in `NAMES` and every value passes its kind |
| allow-listed | `app/Domain/Landing/ThemeTokens.php` | `accepts()`, then `property()` and `cssValue()` map a contract name to a CSS custom property |
| resolved | `app/Features/Landing/ThemeStylesheet.php:53-71` | each accepted pair becomes `property:value`, joined with `;` — **re-validated at the emission point**, deliberately: *"A control that is only correct because its caller is correct is not a control."* |
| handed over | `app/Features/Landing/LandingRenderer.php:55` | `'themeStyle' => ThemeStylesheet::declarations($document->theme)` |
| consumed | `resources/views/landing/page.blade.php:32` | `<html lang="…" dir="…" style="{{ $themeStyle }}">` |

**The rendered page consumes an inline `style` attribute on `<html>`** — custom properties set at the document root, which every rule in the page's own stylesheet then reads. There is no per-tenant stylesheet file and no second renderer.

### B4 — what `packages/tokens` emits, and its scope

Six artefacts in `packages/tokens/generated/`: `tokens.css`, `tokens.ts`, `theme.css`, `panel-theme.css`, `contrast.json`, `contrast.md`.

**All of it is global. None of it is per-tenant.** Checked rather than assumed: the only occurrences of *tenant* under `packages/tokens` are PROSE in comments, and every one of them says the same thing from the other direction — `source.ts:249-251` records that a tenant theme can only ever produce a property in a fixed namespace *"and no tenant token name"* can collide with the product's own. The token build runs once per release; the tenant's values arrive per request, at `page.blade.php:32`.

### B5 — can the contract express a STRUCTURAL difference?

**Yes. It already does, and the mechanism has shipped since `QRPAGER-33`.**

`LandingTemplate` (`app/Domain/Landing/LandingTemplate.php:68, 85`) has two cases — `classic` and `editorial` — and each has its own Blade file under `resources/views/landing/templates/`. It is a member of the DOCUMENT (`template`), validated by `LandingSchema`, and its own docblock states the cost of a third: *"a third arrangement is one case here, one Blade file"*.

So the question's premise — that colour is all the contract can carry — is false. **A preset is a named pair of two members the document already has**: `template` for the structure, `theme` for the colour. rail is a ruled single column, ember a dark centred hero, tile a photo grid; those are three arrangements, and arrangements are exactly what `LandingTemplate` is.

**The smallest addition, as asked: one enum case per preset, plus its Blade file.** Not one new colour column, and not a widening of `ThemeTokens::NAMES` — a conclusion that also cuts against the earlier reading in `§1`'s preset ruling, which assumed `NAMES` would have to widen. It may still need to for a preset's PALETTE (the six-vs-nine-and-ten arithmetic `QRPAGER-40` measured stands), but the STRUCTURAL half needs nothing new at all.

⚠ **AND `TemplateTotalityTest` IS WHY A THIRD CASE IS SAFE TO ADD.** It reads the committed JSON schema and requires every block type to appear in every arrangement's output, so a preset that silently dropped a block the owner had placed fails at the gate rather than on the published page.

### B6 — does any of this need a migration?

**No.**

Both members live inside the existing `jsonb` document, so adding an arrangement changes no column, no type and no constraint. `LandingTemplate`'s docblock makes the distinction explicitly and gives the counter-example: it is deliberately **not** a Postgres enum, because `§2.3`'s convention governs a STORED COLUMN, and `template` is a member of `landing_pages.document` validated by `BlockSchema`/`LandingSchema` — whereas `tenant_language` went the other way at `QRPAGER-30` *"precisely because it IS a column"*.

The committed contract `docs/contracts/landing-page.schema.json:577-586` carries `template` with its `enum` list, and that file is GENERATED from `values()` by `php artisan landing:schema-export` with `bin/landing-schema-check` byte-diffing it. So a new case updates a generated artefact, not a schema.

| **R-009** | **The role password verifier is written to the Postgres log on every bootstrap.** F4 moved the _plaintext_ off the wire; it did not stop a credential reaching the log. Measured across one `db:bootstrap`: 110 new container-log lines, **0** occurrences of the plaintext and **6** of `SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:…` — twice per role, once as the bound parameter `format()` sends and once in the `ALTER ROLE` statement text. The verifier is the complete `pg_authid` secret: `ServerKey` lets an attacker complete a SCRAM handshake **as the server** (and `sslmode=require` does not authenticate the server — R-008), and `StoredKey` enables offline password recovery at 4096 PBKDF2-SHA256 rounds. It is a row rather than a silent fix because the CLASS is worse than the instance: a check that cannot distinguish "I failed to measure" from "the thing is absent" will, in another place, fail in the direction that matters. ### 5.1 Ledger sweep of 2026-10-27 — every row read against its own owner

Run at the start of Task 5, before any Task 5 work, because `§5` had grown to ninety-odd rows
and **every `§11` reviewer reads the table**. The sweep's question was narrow and mechanical:
**is any row owned by a task that is already tagged, and still open?** A row owned by finished
work is either done or mis-owned, and neither of those is "open".

**Counts. Before: 99 rows — 26 closed, 73 open. After the sweep: 99 rows — 30 closed, 69 open.**
**And at the end of Task 5: 103 rows — 34 closed, 69 open**, after the task closed the four rows
it owned (`R-006`, `R-007`, `R-035`, `R-081`) and wrote four (`R-100` … `R-103`). Four of the open
69 are *part*-closed: `R-045`, `R-059`, `R-088`, `R-091`.
No row was created by the sweep; `§11`'s *corrected in place, never as a new risk row* applies
to everything it found.

**⚠ THESE FOUR NUMBERS ARE A CORRECTION. The first draft of this section published "31 → 35
closed, 68 → 64 open" and all four were wrong**, re-measured on 2026-10-28 before any Task 5
implementation commit. The sweep's *effect* is unchanged — it closed exactly four rows — but
the figures around it were taken with a grep and the grep was counting things that are not
closures. Recorded as a correction rather than silently replaced, because `R-025` is the
standing row about exactly this and the defect landing in the sweep's own arithmetic is worth
more than a tidy number.

**The counting rule, stated so the next count is reproducible: a row is CLOSED when nothing
remains for any owner, and OPEN when any part remains, however much of it is done.** By that
rule the table is **30 closed · 69 open**, and **five of the 69 are *part*-closed**: `R-007`
(Task 2's half closed at `2655bdd`, Task 5 still owns the role matrix and the lower-casing),
`R-045` (the "no test covers it" half closed at Task 3, the row stays open for Task 12),
`R-059` (the local half closed at Task 3 ahead of its owner, CI's half still Task 12's),
`R-091` (the `ORDER BY` half done, the figure and the product question still open) and `R-088`
(three of four coverage gaps, see its row).

**Why a grep disagrees, in both directions.** Searching the table for `CLOSED` returns **36**.
Two of those are not closures at all: `R-088`'s new Review-by cell reads **PART-CLOSED**, and
**`R-047` contains the phrase "`/readyz` fails CLOSED with no snapshot"** — a fail-open/fail-closed
posture, not a closure record. `R-047` is **open**, owned by Task 13, and its Review-by is unmet.
The other four of the 36 are the part-closed rows above, which declare a closure and stay open.

**Tags that exist, which is what "already tagged" was measured against:** `task-0`, `task-1`,
`task-2`, `task-3` (`f30bd24`), `task-4` (`55a4f98`). Tasks 3 and 4 are tagged and **not**
merged, by instruction.

#### FLAGGED — a task carrying more deferred work than its own scope

The flag rule is stated rather than felt: **a remaining task is flagged when its open-row
count exceeds twice the remaining-task mean (45.4).** One task does.

**⚠ `Task 12` — SECURITY HARDENING — CARRIES 74 OPEN ROWS.** That is **3.3× the
remaining-task mean**, **54% of every open row owned by a remaining task**, more than twice

exists to catch**, and `§3.2`'s twentieth delta already saw its leading edge from the
row-by-row side — it swept `R-141`…`R-170` and found *"eleven owned weakly or partly, all
of them to Task 12"*. Read by owner the pattern is not eleven rows, it is **seventy-four**:

owns it"* has been the cheapest honest-looking disposition available at every review since

## 6. Open items

- Billing / subscriptions: not in the Blueprint and not requested by the client. **Out of scope until stated.**
- Launch tier: unset by design until Task 14.
- **Queue transport for push dispatch.** The Blueprint specified SQS. The design is an outbox table plus a worker, which satisfies the guarantee — "ready" commits instantly, the send happens behind it with retries — independently of transport. Laravel's Redis queue is the default. **Task 13 decides whether the launch tier needs SQS instead, and Task 14 measures it.** Do not assume either.
- **Data migrations under FORCE RLS — settled, and corrected.** The pattern is `PLAN.md §2.10`. It was wrong until 2026-10-25 (H-1, QA review of task-1): it opened by enumerating tenants with a plain owner read, which returns **zero rows** under FORCE RLS, so the loop body never ran and a backfill would have silently done nothing. The list now comes through one audited `withoutTenantScope()` read; the per-tenant work still needs no bypass. `DataMigrationPatternTest` proves both halves, including at transaction level 1, which is where every migration body runs.
- **`outbox` and `audit_log` retention is unassigned.** Both grow without bound (§2.11): no grant deletes a `sent` or `dead` outbox row, and `audit_log` is append-only, so pruning it can only ever be a partition drop, never a `DELETE`. Nothing breaks before launch; it is a disk bill that grows. **Decide in Task 13 (storage sizing) and measure in Task 14.** Do not let the first person who notices invent a `DELETE`, because the trigger will refuse it.
- **Platform-admin cross-tenant reads are not on the §4 named list.** Task 6 builds a platform dashboard, a restaurants list and an audit-log viewer, all of which read across tenants. `§4 › Tenancy` names exactly four cross-tenant paths and says "adding one requires editing this file first". Task 1 deliberately built **no** policy for these: `qrpager_app` has no cross-tenant policy anywhere. Task 6 must either get §4 amended (a rank-2 edit, so the user's call) or go through §2.8's `SECURITY DEFINER` recipe with its own authorisation. **Raised now so Task 6 does not discover it mid-wizard.**
- **Platform-scope `audit_log` rows (`tenant_id` NULL) can currently be written only through the owner bypass.** `app` holds `INSERT` but the isolation policy's `WITH CHECK` compares `tenant_id` to the context, and `NULL = x` is never true. Task 6's "platform admin actions all land in `audit_log`" therefore needs a decision: an `INSERT`-only policy allowing `tenant_id IS NULL` (write-only for the app, readable only through §2.8), or every platform action naming a tenant. Not invented here.
- **Laravel wraps the driver error — settled at Task 2 (`2655bdd`, wired in at `ccca185`).** `QueryException::getCode()` is not reliably the SQLSTATE, and the shape of the unreliability is now measured rather than warned about: for STATEMENT errors `getCode()` and `getPrevious()->errorInfo[0]` **agree** — `42P01`, `22P02`, `22012` — which is exactly why a `getCode()`-based reader looks correct. For a CONNECTION-level failure they do not: a refused connection and a wrong password both give `getCode()` = the integer **`7`** where the SQLSTATE is **`08006`**. So anything built on `getCode()` printed "SQLSTATE 7" for precisely the failures an operator most needs named — and `08006` is also how a saturated role `CONNECTION LIMIT` arrives at the client, never `53300`. `App\Platform\Database\DriverError` is the single reader: `sqlState()` walks the chain for a `PDOException` with an `errorInfo`, and `sqlStateForMessage()` returns a real SQLSTATE or an empty string rather than a wrong code. `tests/TestCase.php::sqlState()` keeps the same shape for the suite.

### API versioning — the policy for a breaking change

Written here at Task 2, which the `§3` gate requires ("the versioning policy for a breaking change is
written into §6") and `D6` places in this file rather than in `PROJECT_INSTRUCTIONS.md §6`: it is a
project decision, not a universal rule, so it belongs at rank 3.

**The surface.** Every public API route is under `/v1`, served by `bootstrap/app.php`'s
`apiPrefix: 'v1'`. Enforced by `tests/Feature/Http/RouteSurfaceTest.php`, which fails on any public
route outside `/v1` that is not in a written allowlist.

**The two exceptions, and why they are not versioned.** `/healthz` and `/readyz`. A load balancer's
health-check path is infrastructure configuration, and versioning it means the target group has to be
reconfigured because the API's major version changed — a deploy-time coupling with no benefit. They are
on their own middleware group, carrying no rate limiter, no tenant middleware and no load shedding,
which is the mechanism behind `§4 › Edge & ops`'s "while health and readiness keep answering". Approved
by the user on 2026-10-26, after confirming that nothing called the route being replaced: Laravel's
`/up` was referenced in exactly one place outside `vendor/` — `bootstrap/app.php` — and by no
healthcheck, no CI step, no test and no document.

**A published path is never changed in place.** Once a path under `/v1` has been deployed, its
behaviour may only be extended compatibly. The following are **breaking** and may not be done to a
published path:

| Breaking | Compatible |
| --- | --- |
| removing or renaming a field in a response | adding a field |
| narrowing an accepted input, or making an optional field required | widening an accepted input, or adding an optional field |
| changing a field's type, or the meaning of a value | adding a value to an enum **only** where the client is specified to ignore unknown values |
| changing a status code for an existing outcome | adding a status code for a new outcome |
| removing a route, or changing what a path matches | adding a route |

**How a breaking change ships.** A new prefix — `/v2` — carrying only the routes that change. `/v1`
keeps working until it is retired. The two live side by side; there is no "upgrade in place" path, and
no version negotiation by header: the version is in the path, where a CDN, a log line and a WAF rule
can all see it. Retiring `/v1` is its own decision with its own notice period, taken when a tenant is
actually on `/v2`.

**The enum caveat is not theoretical.** `pager_status` is a shared contract generated into
`packages/contracts` at Task 8 (ADR-003) from the PHP enum. Adding a case is a **breaking** change to
any client that switches exhaustively on it, which a TypeScript client does by default. So a new
`pager_status` value is a `/v2` change unless the client contract states that unknown values map to a
documented fallback — a decision for the task that adds the case, recorded with it.

**What enforces this.** The committed OpenAPI document. CI regenerates it from the routes and fails on
a diff, so a breaking change cannot reach `main` without appearing in a reviewed spec diff. The
document is the record of what was published; this policy is what may be done to it.
